name: Heartland Beef
blurb: One big packing plant in Prairie Bend, 1,400 line workers, and about 600 ranches that sell it cattle. Founder Walt Dreyer started as a rancher and holds 28% of the vote.

directors.name: Carla Whitfield
directors.title: Attorney
directors.motive: You reviewed the Premium Program terms and told Heartland the opt-in language was enough. You have since read the complaints.

exposure.text: You are disbarred if the board is caught hiding a heavy fact.
exposure.label: Disbarred if caught hiding

secrets.text: Clean the books: the board admits every fact in round 1.
secrets.label: Admit every fact in round 1

secrets.text: Your firm bills Heartland $2M a year for its contract work. One caught fact ends it, so none may be caught.
secrets.label: No fact gets caught

directors.name: Denise Kowalski
directors.title: Labor director
directors.motive: Your members cut the beef, and the buyers who push quotas are their neighbors. You have seen what a missed quota does to a family.

exposure.text: Members vote you out if $60M goes to TraceMark while their raise stays frozen.
exposure.label: TraceMark funded

secrets.text: Your members' retirement plan holds Heartland stock. The stock must end above where it started.
secrets.label: Stock ends above start

directors.name: Marcus Feld
directors.title: Fund partner
directors.motive: Cornbelt's investors want growth, and sign-up numbers have been the growth chart. TraceMark is the kind of story that lifts a price.

exposure.text: Your investors pull their money if the stock ends below where it started.
exposure.label: Stock ends below start

secrets.text: Your fund holds a stake in the nephew's startup. TraceMark must pass.
secrets.label: TraceMark passes

secrets.text: Your fund quietly owns a rival packer. The stock must finish in the bottom half.
secrets.label: Stock ends in bottom half

directors.name: Gus Halvorsen
directors.title: Founder's friend
directors.home: Walt Dreyer, the founder (hunting partner of 30 years)
directors.motive: Walt has never been wrong about cattle in the thirty years you have hunted together. He has never been right about software, but he has never lost an argument about it.

exposure.text: You lose the seat if the board votes down TraceMark, which Walt wants.
exposure.label: TraceMark voted down

secrets.text: Walt signed off on the buyer quotas. The board must never admit every fact about them in round 1.
secrets.label: Don't admit every fact in round 1

secrets.text: Walt's name is on the TraceMark deal and on the quota memo. No fact on this board may be caught.
secrets.label: No fact gets caught

directors.name: Luanne Pruitt
directors.title: Community seat (Ranchers' co-op president)
directors.motive: You lead the ranchers' co-op, and some Premium fees came out of your members' checks. You have also sold Heartland your own cattle for years.

exposure.text: You face a no-confidence vote at home if the quotas stay.
exposure.label: Quotas stay

secrets.text: TraceMark fails and the money goes to rancher refunds instead.
secrets.label: TraceMark fails

secrets.text: Buyers chasing quota pay your 4,000-head feedlot the best price in the county. The quotas stay.
secrets.label: Quotas stay

motions.title: End buyer sign-up quotas and refund Premium Program fees
motions.motive: Stop paying people to sign up ranchers who did not ask.

headline.passed: Heartland ends buyer quotas and refunds ranchers
headline.failed: Heartland keeps quotas despite rancher complaints

issue.text: To hit quotas, some Heartland cattle buyers enrolled ranchers in a paid Premium Program. The hotline logged 212 complaints last year. HR reviewed some and calls most of them misunderstandings.
issue.case_for_silence: Most complaints may be misunderstandings, ranchers did sign something, and ending the program would blow a hole in this year's numbers.

facts.text: The hotline logged 212 complaints from ranchers about Premium Program fees they did not expect.
Buyers get bonuses for sign-ups and lose their jobs for missing quota.
HR reviewed some complaints and called most of them misunderstandings.
Board reports mentioned sign-up growth but not the complaints.

motions.title: Put $60M into the founder's TraceMark system and announce it to buyers
motions.motive: Tracing is the future, and Walt has never missed on cattle.

headline.failed: Heartland board turns down founder's TraceMark bet

issue.text: Founder Walt Dreyer wants $60M for TraceMark, a cattle-tracing system built by his nephew's startup. It has run only in demos. Nobody on the board has run a tracing system.
issue.case_for_silence: Demos are how every new system starts, the engineers may have left for ordinary reasons, and public doubt could kill a bet that may pay.

facts.text: No one on the board has run a tracing system or read its test data.
TraceMark has only been shown in demos run by Walt's nephew's team.
Two TraceMark engineers left last spring, and the startup calls it ordinary turnover.
No outside lab has tested it.

cases.line: Wells Fargo paid $185M in 2016 over unauthorized accounts. Its board heard of the risk in 2014 but got incomplete numbers.
Theranos raised over $700M. Its founder was sentenced in 2022 to 11 years 3 months. Critics noted a board of famous names with little medical expertise.

real.fix: Ask for the raw numbers, and seat directors who can read them.
